Although she replaced it, Waitress completely disinterested and made excuse for kitchen saying “they’re very busy today.”Should also mention booked through my American Express Platinum FHR.Hotel provides only $60 for breakfast which is totally not enough.FYI, hotel sets the dollar amount allocated so they are knowingly being stingy!Mentioned all of the above on the way out, (after waiting 15+ minutes to check out because they only had 3 agents working at the desk!) and the girl said she was sorry….. that’s it.Other than being new and shiny, there is nothing that makes this hotel fancy or upscale.Go elsewhere…..we will next trip.

reviews.title: Boring and no customers.
reviews.text: This has to be the most boring resort on the planet. The casino was like a ghost town. One minute they offer rates with no resort fees the next minute they want to charge resort fees. Why email people offer rates with no resort fees then you try to book they want the resort fees. I decided to try the hotel for one night. It was a big mistake as even though the rooms were nice I couldn’t get over how they offer rates with no resort fees then they charge resort fees. The location is also miles away from most of the action on the Vegas Strip. If this resort wants to stay in business it needs to work out how to attract people to stay because at the moment the place is empty.

reviews.title: Everything is top notch.
reviews.text: It’s a great property. The rooms are obviously new and clean and they have great touches like automatic drapes and a bar set and refrigerated drawer. The hotel goes above and beyond to make guests comfortable. The pool is wonderful- even the handrails are stylish. And there’s ample shade from the desert sun provided by umbrellas at nearly every lounger. Unlike many Vegas resorts, there is no fee for them. There’s a great selection of restaurants- they’re a little pricey but not outside the normal range of other strip hotels. The location is perfect for conventions, but it is a long distance from center strip. Walking is not really an option, if not for the distance for the time one would have to account for.

reviews.title: Strike 3
reviews.text: Currently on the 3rd day of a 4 night stay at the Fontainbleau and will not be returning.•Started off on the wrong foot upon checking in.  Booked thru AMEX FHR.Agent who checked us in, (younger girl with braces but forgot her name) insisted that we weren't entitled to breakfast on the last day because "it wasn't considered a full day."  Told her I've booked with AMEX FHR about 75-80 times over the years including 2 previous times at this hotel but she continued to beligerantly insist she was correct.  Asked her to have a Mgr call me or my room to conform.  No call.  Had to resolve it myself and obviously she was completely misinformed.• Speaking of AMEX FHR, the hotel only allocates $60 for breakfast, which is the bare minimum required by AMEX.  Unfortunately, the amount  allocated by the hotel is completely insufficient for the free breakfast perk from AMEX  Does not adequately cover breakfast at Vida, In addition, the so-called breakfast menu at Vida is breakfast AND lunch; even at 8am!...But hey, it'll at least cover a bagel and coffee.  (Sarcasm)•NO water at all provided in the room. (Was 108° here yesterday •Fitness Center closes at 7pm, unheard of and inexcusable at a casino hotel.• Surprisingly, no turn-down service.• No cushions on chaises at pool,nor an attendant that sets you up.•Surprisingly, (again!),  nowhere to eat after 10pm(Only Chez Bon Bon is 24 hours; great if you want dessert or a bagel but not good if you want real food after 10 o'clock)This is the 3td trip here and will be the last.  As someone who spends 70+ nights in a hotel annually and all for leisure, sometimes 2 or 3 little issues is as unpleasant as 1 big issue.While the Fontainbleau is new and glitzy, you're getting the same service and extras you'd find in a plain old 3-star Marriott. Zero chance the family will be returning.....way too many other options in Vegas

reviews.title: From Vegas with Love ❤️
reviews.text: Magnificent from start to finish just go no regrets 5***** across the board location unique absolutely service and amenities fabulous loved it

reviews.title: Treat Yourself. Book it here.
reviews.text: We stayed at the noble one bedroom suite. If you are big on immaculate rooms, amazing, attentive staff, and awesome pools, this is it. This is an absolutely stunning top tier hotel. What an experience.

reviews.title: It's a very excellent hotel and casino...
reviews.text: They have a very nice bed and pillows, very excellent room service,a very nice bathroom, nice bath tub and a beautiful shower...

reviews.title: Dirty-no customer service
reviews.text: Check-in took over 20 minutes, which was frustrating after a long day of travel. To be fair, the gentleman at the counter was very polite and professional. However, once we got to our room, things quickly went downhill.We found what appeared to be multiple pubic hairs — in the shower, near the toilet, on the carpet, and even one on the bed. To make matters worse, there seemed to be a dried booger on the door. Completely unacceptable for any hotel, let alone one claiming to be five-star. I immediately called to speak with a manager. He said he would find us another room, but that took another 20 minutes.Eventually, we were handed a key to a new room, but at no point did anyone offer an apology or acknowledge how unpleasant this experience was. I expected much more in terms of cleanliness, efficiency, and basic hospitality.

reviews.title: Luxury Experience
reviews.text: This is my third time staying at this hotel and it never disappoints. The staff and service are so friendly and helpful. I have also noticed that compared to other hotels, the smoke smell is practically non existent (my allergies don't flare up at all) and all the machines are clean. All the dining experiences are top notch. Room is always clean.

reviews.title: Wonderful experience with lots of fun.
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel with the best service I have ever encountered. The casino was beautiful and I enjoyed the dealer at the roulette table named Courtney.  I will be back.

reviews.title: Great place to relax
reviews.text: Great place to go to relax and play slots. Very clean and welcoming. The atmosphere is great and it's my favorite place to stay when I go to Vegas.

reviews.title: I shall return
reviews.text: EXCELLENT. I have travelled all over the world and have stayed in some OK places. But the experience at Fontainebleau is second to none. we had our doors opened for us. 1st impression. Atmosphere and reception of staff was exceptionally pleasant. Had it not been my birthday, I could have stayed in the room all weekend. Modern and comfortable. Fontainebleau went all out on the decor.

reviews.title: Beautiful hotel with all the amenties!
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel that smelled of roses from the moment you walk in! Spacious rooms, large tub, beds are comfy and all this with stunning views! The fitness center is superb with eceptional customer service. Do not hesitate to book this incredible hotel!

reviews.title: Pool Life
reviews.text: Fantastic experience, we definitely plan to go back! The hotel was gorgeous! We spent the day at the pool and absolutely loved our pool day!

reviews.title: The best stay ever.
reviews.text: The beds are very comfortable and clean. The restaurant food was superb and the services that was provided during our stay was very good.

reviews.title: Stay at Aria or Cosmo instead. Overpriced on everything and just not worth it.
reviews.text: I came in with very high hopes the property looked beautiful from the photos online. When we arrived at the hotel check-in went smooth and I tipped the receptionist $100. In the 40 years of coming to Las Vegas as an adult and tipping a receptionist this was a new standard. She handed each of us a mini bottle of water. We made our way up to the room 3533 it has a nice view of the strip. For a suite and what it cost I really wish we had booked the Aria instead we both agreed. We wanted something to eat so made our way to the “Promenade” signs said scan this QR code to order…well that didn’t work and the line to get a sandwich was 12 people deep. Ok…let’s just get something out by the pool, we were directed to LaCote. It looked nice enough we sat and ordered two sandwiches. As we were waiting it became obvious there were cleanliness issues. Food debris on the floor under tables, food debris on the bench seating next to me and on multiple other ones. The place only had a handful of diners yet the adjacent table remained uncleaned until halfway through our meal. Food came  yes they didn’t get one of the side orders correctly but alas this happens. We signed for our food It was $80 for two sandwiches and drinks, and returned to the room and locked the door to take a nap. 20 minutes later a knock on the door from “mini bar”. We let in the attendant who proceeded to refill the mini bar that had apparently been used by the previous guests. One would think that would have been done before new guests arrived. The hotel really does screw you on food prices. A morning coffee, latte and two pastries was $44 with tip (the were great pastries and we joked they must have been made offsite). Dinner at "the tavern" which is the sports book was $150. The property is pretty, The bellman out front were great. I'm in a wheelchair and they were always super helpful in and out of taxi's. For what the hotel costs vs what you get stay someplace else. They are billed as a high end resort and they are not. There is no contact email anyplace for customer service. I think that says a lot. They want your money and that's it. To many nice hotels in vegas to waste your money at this place.

reviews.title: A little disappointed
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, rooms are comfortable. I was able to check in earlier that was nice; saying that,  The front desk needs help in Costumer service, they are not too friendly or helpful. When i arrived to my room it was dirty, red sticky substance on the counter that spilled into the dresser , for the amount per night and the resorts fees, this hotel room needs to be spotless. The toiletries were empty when we arrived , it wasn't replaced.  Beautiful building, I'm not sure if I would go back again

reviews.title: Great Hotel!!
reviews.text: Best hotel we've stayed in. Our new place. Amazing service, feel safe, great staff, easy to check in and some of the best restaurants in the area. Great vibe too. Not crazy.

reviews.title: Great destination for a wonderful stay and things to do.
reviews.text: Great destination for a stay with very comfortable rooms and peaceful atmosphere. This place is huge and has many options for all tastes.

reviews.title: Excellent Addition to the  Las Vegas Strip
reviews.text: My wife & I stayed at Fontainebleau Las Vegas from June 29 to July 1, 2025. We stayed in room 58-811, which is classified as a Bleau King Mountain Best view room. Overall, since this hotel is quite new, everything in the room was in excellent condition. The room decor was modern & clean with minimalist touches. All the light and curtain controls are capacitive touch buttons that work quite well. The bed was very comfy and the water pressure of the shower was quite strong. The room size was also larger than we expected. The best comparison to the room size and quality is the Conrad at Resorts World (which is also quite nice). The best amenity that we experienced at this resort was its gym. It was absolutely gigantic, but also state-of-the-art. Everything was there for our workouts. It’s a must visit if you’re staying at this resort!Based on such a positive experience we had, we will definitely be back next time we visit Las Vegas!

reviews.title: Wonderful and amazing experience!
reviews.text: Everything was excellent. We arrived in Las Vegas on a late flight and found that only the property's bars were open. A 24-hour restaurant would be a valuable amenity. We decided to dine off property instead. In every other respect, our experience was amazing.

reviews.title: Elegant Relaxation
reviews.text: Best place to stay on the strip! Fountainbleau truly has it all. Elegant and comfortable rooms, spacious pool with plenty of shade, fun games, delicious eats. I could spend my whole stay in Las Vegas at the Fountainebleau and be absolutely satisfied.

reviews.title: Good experience within FB but limited option to venture out during hot summer
reviews.text: Good facility, friendly staff, a little far away from casinos visit. the strip which made the walk too tired so I'll miss other

reviews.title: Holiday July 2025
reviews.text: We have previously stayed at Wynn annd Encore  and I thought that they were the best in Vegas. Not anymore Fontainebleau has exceeded our expectations and we cannot wait to return. The rooms are too die for, pool’s excellent and the restaurants are amazing. Could not fault it at all !!

reviews.title: FountainBleu Vegas beats all expectations
reviews.text: Room was super nice and spotless. Mother Wolff had some of the best pasta’s I have ever eaten outside of Italy. And Chez Bon Bon is great for coffee/pastries/gelato

reviews.title: My Place to Stay!
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful! The attention paid to detail is extraordinary. The service was above and beyond! Everyone is very friendly and helpful. I love staying here!

reviews.title: Chic hotel
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel! Every square inch is spotless and tastefully decorated. It's a very minimalistic, chic vibe. Fabulous restaurants and shopping. Rooms are beautiful, especially love the bathrobe

reviews.title: Beware of Flying Pool Umbrellas!
reviews.text: We stayed over 4th of July weekend. The hotel pools (6) are fabulous and a reason to stay there. The management of the hotel is absolutely horrible. My nephew was hit by a flying pool umbrella during a wind gust and was injured in the chest (as were two other guests).  We were checked by paramedics at the pool. The pool security and management  would only take our name and room number. They would not fill out a report. My nephew’s bruised and scratched chest grew bigger as the stay went on. I tried to get an accident report but the desk told us we could write what happened and they would print that and nothing else. Two times I went back and spoke with the front desk. At checkout  I mentioned it again and they comped two of the three $50 resort fees. However, when I arrived home, the charges were put back on. When I asked why, they said that it is their policy that we had to sign a release preventing us from taking further action for the $100.   What a horrible management/customer service team. This is a huge Vegas hotel, not some mom and pop place. It was their umbrella that hit us. They failed to secure their equipment properly.  I have stayed at multiple hotels on the strip. The customer service was incredible at every other hotel. As far as the hotel itself, the room  was beautiful.  The bathroom is gorgeous but the floors had hair on them and the toilet had water stains. We had a view of the parking lot, so we could see fireworks from downtown but not from the strip. The food throughout the hotel whether at a bar, restaurant, pool or food court was delicious. Expect to pay $25 for a frozen margarita, $15 for a soda without refills, $12 for a beer. A big drawback is the location on the strip. There is a bus stop across the street for $8/24hrs. Otherwise, a taxi or Uber will cost you $30-$50 during prime time to get where you are going. We paid $90 round trip for dinner one night, $30 each way to/from the airport in a taxi, $86 for a trip home from the stadium after a concert. There is a convenience store across the street, a Walgreens .4 miles from the hotel. There are a lot of unhoused people heading towards Walgreens and downtown.

reviews.title: Great time at FB
reviews.text: We loved our stay. The rooms were amazing and the bedding was heavenly. We slept really well. We loved eating at Vida and Komodo.

reviews.title: Wait, Vegas Is This Classy??
reviews.text: You will not find a resort in Vegas where you can have the Vegas experience, but feel like you are in a high end resort near an ocean destination. EVERY single employee loves their job, everything everywhere is spotless clean! Just like living in a dream. You MUST try it. WE have stayed there 5 times so far. Totally in on this place!!!!!

reviews.title: Wonder Experience
reviews.text: Great experience at a first rate hotel and Casio .  Rooms were exceptional and reasonably priced.  Staff was friendly and attentive

reviews.title: Fontainebleau is definitely worth a stay in Las Vegas
reviews.text: We returned to the Fontainebleau because of our previous positive experience there. Although we knew it was kind of far north, it seemed further away from the action this time. We returned because of the value, as well as being able to rent a car there without having any airport hassle. I tried three great restaurants, The Tavern, for deli type foods, Washing Potato for excellent Asian, and finally Mother Wolf for the bread! Overall, a great place to stay/play -just a quick 10 minute walk to the Wynn!

reviews.title: Roses Fontainebleau
reviews.text: For this July 4th long weekend in Las Vegas, we kicked things off with a stay at the Fontainebleau—and wow, what a structure. It’s massive, sleek, and hard to miss. I heard it’s one of the newest hotels on the Strip, and it definitely felt that way.The lobby made quite the impression—with a striking display of fresh roses that added a touch of opulence to the already glamorous space. Our room was lovely, with a stunning view of the city lights at night.✨You can tell it’s new by the small details—modern finishes, updated layouts—but also some curious things, like the quietness of the hotel and the not-so-obvious presence of cameras. It made me pause and wonder. Oh, and true to Vegas style, the lobby connects straight into the casino floor.It was a short but sweet stay at the Fontainebleau—and a unique start to our Vegas weekend. 💫🎲#FontainebleauLasVegas #VegasVibes #July4Weekend #VegasStrip #NewHotelFeel #CityLightsView #VegasLuxury #TravelWithMira #MiRasMoments #VegasGetaway #ModernLuxury #ShortStaySweetMemories #DesertLights #Vegas2025

reviews.title: First time there had a great time.
reviews.text: It was pretty cool. Checking in wasn’t bad at all I pretty much got serviced immediately. The guy at the front counter was also pretty chill. Told him it was my first time here and gave me a late checkout to really enjoy my time there. When I entered my room everything was pretty neat. Blinds opened by themselves when you first walk in. All controls are on the wall. Many outlets and a big tv. The main area where the casino and stores and restaurants are located. Was massive and a lot of fancy stores like Graff, Cartier, and etc. many cool restaurants. The pools don’t have anything that cool like mandalay but it’s still really good. I was there during July 4-6 since I was there for The Weeknd concert.

reviews.title: Fontainebleau should not be overlooked!
reviews.text: Wonderful property with terrific amenities, staff and food options. Yes, it's for North on the strip and this turns some people off but I have been going to Vegas multiple times for many years and I am not a "strip Walker". From FB I can easily catch a ride-share and go anywhere easily. Location is not an issue for me. As I said, the food options are terrific. The staff is friendly and helpful. Property is clean and fresh looking. Pool is great. Yes, it's not inexpensive but it is worth it IMO.

reviews.title: Luxury addition to Vegas!
reviews.text: Amazing luxurious hotel, good location  where you can easily access the strip and Freemont street. So many options available at the hotel that you don’t really need to leave!! The rooms are spacious and tastefully decorated with good views, and staff are very helpful and friendly. The hotel also offers a good rewards programme. I will definitely return again in future!

reviews.title: security and lack of trained personnel and poor maintenance on casino equipment
reviews.text: very bad security that let dangerous people into the floors who also urinated against doors and carpets in our hallway on the 53rd floor. Be careful when visiting

reviews.title: $4,685 Stay, But Charged Extra for a Kettle  Not Worth It
reviews.text: We booked a 9-night stay in one of the hotel’s premium suites and spent nearly $4,685.43 expecting a high-end, comfortable experience. Instead, we were shocked by the lack of basic hospitality and the way the hotel tries to squeeze money out of guests.We were asked to pay $22 just to rent a simple water kettle, and the same went for a coffee machine both of which are standard, complimentary items in even the most basic hotels. Charging for these during a long 9-night stay felt absurd, especially for the price we’re already paying.This isn’t about the money  it’s about how it made us feel. When you pay this much, you expect generosity, not petty charges and poor guest care.If you’re looking for true luxury or thoughtful service, I’d strongly reconsider booking here. Our experience was disappointing and frustrating, and we won’t be coming back.

reviews.title: Great concert venue
reviews.text: I visited here for the Jennifer Hudson Christmas concert and it was a great choice for the concert. Once inside, the venue wasn’t too crowded and it was accessible. The only thing is the walk from the entrance of the hotel to the concert area, it was longer than expected.

reviews.title: Short stay in Las Vegas after Utah Park trip
reviews.text: The Hotel is outstanding . It's has a laid back upscale vibe not found in other hotels . Not crowded due to the large amount of space. Great food at all restaurants we tried. Fantastic pool area. A bit removed from the main strip and shopping ,but I think that is a plus. Rooms are 1st rate. Would highly recommend .

reviews.title: The Fontainebleau Experience
reviews.text: We came for a conference which we do every year but to my surprise this resort was the cleanest that I have ever been in Vegas, also the security was amazing with top notch service. The Spa is the best so far I have been in Vegas and Papi steakhouse Wao!!! You better come to this Resort if you want to experience the Wao factor!Amazing Expo Hall Space!!!

reviews.title: No blues at Fontainebleau!
reviews.text: I almost want to keep it a secret!!! Fontainebleau is anazing in all of the ways that a hotel can be. The best part is that if you’re anything like me, there is no need to leave! Service, 10! Room, 10! Restaurants, 10! And the pool is a 10 too! The aesthetic of the hotel is beautiful inside & out! I won’t stay anywhere else at this point!

reviews.title: Bachelorette getaway
reviews.text: The room was clean and well prepared. The beds are super comfortable. They spare no expense even on the T3 hairdryers provided in the rooms. All of the staff are friendly and helpful and quick to accommodate their guests throughout their stay. I will be returning as long as they keep up with this stellar service and clean environment!

reviews.title: Maintains its brand new charm
reviews.text: The hotel still keeps its brand new feel. Beautiful hotel and rooms with a very comfortable bed, fluffy pillows and crisp sheets.

reviews.title: Great hotel
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel! So clean, friendly staff, huge rooms. We stayed for three nights and this hotel feels really comfortable. The AC is quiet and efficient, beds are comfy, linens have no weird smells.We had brunch at Lafontaine - delicious. Steak and eggs and lemon pancakes were both fantastic. Service very friendly. Bagel restaurant in the promenade is nice for a quick snack in the early morning. Supper at Don's prime was great too. Filet and strip loin both cooked perfectly. If you're making a reservation here it will offer a set menu, but be aware this is only until 6:30pm. This used to be stated on the reservation page but when we booked it was not so I assumed there were no time limitations. The first server was pretty cold when he told us this - the second was really friendly and made up for it. Maybe that's a thing they do? Anyways glad we just ordered off the menu as everything was delicious. Will definitely visit again. It's fun to walk to the arts district and breweries and stop at the Sahara on the way for a bit of roulette/blackjack. 10$ tables in the afternoon.

reviews.title: Gorgeous building, poor service
reviews.text: Gorgeous building, poor service.  Understaffed to shocking levels, indifferent to guests.  Overpriced food, many amenities not open or rarely open.  Restaurants not as good as some of the other resorts.  Pool Day Passes being sold absolutely ruins the vibe and cleanliness of the pools.  If you like trashy people and tons of screaming splashing kids, by all means book a room.

reviews.title: Mixed feelings
reviews.text: The hotel itself is beautiful. Everything looks nice and clean professional and five star. As you go deeper into the hotel and experience the staff the service that ambience and other guests you’ll notice the cracks and the inconsistency and discrimination on how they treat each guest. my experience was 50-50. I would either get great service or very rude and inconsistent service encountered many people who are kind and many of the staff that was very disrespectful. I felt like I was more in a security building rather than a resort like hotel, and my experience was not the best. It’s hard to say all the positive things how beautiful the room was how comfortable the beds were how clean it was because it gets tainted and overshadowed by how some people treated us. It’s an  overpriced prison with snotty employees.

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.text: Love our experience. The staff were so attentive, friendly, and professional. One of the best bathrooms in Las Vegas. Shout out to Monica front desk and Claudia front desk for giving us their best service. We loved our time on the pool and the gym. It was so cleaned and so nice. Cafe cuto is so recommended. We will be back

reviews.title: Fontainebleau - The Epitome Of Luxury
reviews.text: I encountered Fontainebleau in June of 2012, sitting there vacant. I have been fascinated with the hotel ever since. After reading that Fontainebleau has been finished and open for business since December 2023, I had to come stay at Fontainebleau. Staying at this hotel was a life impacting experience, that I will never forget. Staying in a suite on the 61st floor, looking down at the pools at night, was a dream like experience. Housekeeping would come TWICE a day. Who does that? Top notch providers do that. Everything about my experience and my wife's experience at Fontainebleau was phenomenal. The Lapis Spa was incredible. My wife got the best massage she has ever experienced at Lapis Spa.  We took lots of photos and will cherish our four days at this hotel for years to come.

reviews.title: It’s giving “The Price is Right”
reviews.text: We usually always stay at Palazzo which we love, but we wanted to try the new spot in town. It was meh. It was a nice hotel, but for the price, there are better options. The  decor was boring and was giving  a mix between a mall and the set of The Price is Right. The pool area was probably their best asset. The eating choices were meh. We ate breakfast at Vida, which was pretty good. There wasn’t anywhere else exciting. They have a promenade with some fast food choices that were equally unexciting. The rooms were nice but not very spacious. We did have a nice view of the strip and the mountains through the floor to ceiling windows. The shower was small. Another drawback is our hallway smelled incredibly strong of weed our entire stay. Even though they have a strong no smoking policy.The absolute worst part of this hotel was the location. Not only is there little action on this part of the strip, but it’s across the street from the Golden Nugget which is very run down. You have to walk a nice long distance to get to anything else and the ambience in the area is depressing. Won’t be staying here again.

reviews.title: Taste of Fountainblue Las Vegas only
reviews.text: Recently tried 4 restaurants from the Taste of Fountainblue which started June 16- September something I think, similar to Canda's Summerlicious, i.e, set menu on a fixed price;1. La Fontaine-  $ 75.00 tip extra..we were 3 so tried all on the menu.deviled eggs, ok gourmand average; crude enjoyed by group; smoked salmon on brioche (bread not fresh-breaking apart) lemon hollandaise, very good; cheeseburger only touched the meat, fries were tasty but not hot; chocolate ParisBrest amazing as always, should be a bigger slice; soufflé pancake not as good as the last time...BTW all the meals came out so fast, we were wondering if they were already premade. Place was about 25 % occupied.2. Dons Prime - $ 125.- I think I did not pay for this; again with 3 of us we tried all on the menu;crab cake excellent as with the salads; filet mignon undercooked; halibut quite tasty; organic chicken not the greatest; brûlée was good.  Place about 30% occupied.3 Washing potato - $ 65. or $ 75. did not pay for this was disappointed with the amuse bouche of a pineapple bun ( all oriental bakeries have this); maybe soup or spring roll or something; nothing special about the dims trio; beef noodle , walnut shrimp and gailan please just get the walnut shrimp--BTW ver small portions....not worth to do this one.   50% occupied4 Komodo- ginger salad and salmon appetizer fresh and tasty,chilean sea bass was the best; not so much for the stir fry and mushroom noodles; with beans, rice and Brussel sprouts....everything was quite tasty but then minuscule in portions.   25% occupiedIt was a great idea and priced right for a 3 course meal, during this stay. Doing reservations on line was also not very good, since you do not get an answer right away. So we cancelled our online reservations and just walked in. Service at all were always great, filled water glasses and decent.It was a great attraction, so you have a fixed set price, and try the dishes. We are coming back agin in.August, to try the other restos.

reviews.title: An Experience….
reviews.text: My stay at Fontainebleau Las Vegas was absolutely amazing! From the fresh red roses in the lobby to the beautiful smells throughout the air Fontainbleau left no stone unturned… the room was huge, bed was comfy, the shower was fantastic. The staff were incredibly welcoming and went above and beyond to assist me with everything I needed. The food at Vida was delicious and sweet treats at Chez Bon Bon didn’t disappoint! I especially enjoyed the pools and wellness classes. If you’re looking for a luxurious experience look no further Fontainbleau Las Vegas is it! I highly recommend this hotel and will definitely be back!

reviews.title: Family visit to Vegas.
reviews.text: Wonderful, clean hotel with great dining and drinking options. Collin’s bar was amazing. Great atmosphere with the piano. Limited choice of machine gaming on the casino floor and pool a little crowded.

reviews.title: Beautiful hotel, but lack basic standard needs
reviews.text: no 24 hours pool, no sauna or steam unless you pay $180 to use the spa area,  staff is nice but is clueless anytime you ask them a question concerning the hotel, restaurants close way to early.  The hotel is very clean, they have a perfumish scent through the hotel(didn't like that at all, very nauseating)

reviews.title: Poor quality and high price.
reviews.text: To my disappointment, as I was checking to my room and it was not  clean. It had debris in the carpet and the night stand table with stains from the previous guests. The bathroom seem to have the same issues. After two calls to the hotel front desk they finally had it cleaned but not the night table, I had to clean it my self. The Dons restaurant service was good but not our steaks, again disappointment at their food. When we check out, I addressed the issue and what I received from the management they would look in to it. For a resort that supposedly is the high end it is not.

reviews.title: The Fontainebleau Experience
reviews.text: Fontainebleau gave me a 10/10 experience! Everything from the parking garage to the hotel lobby to the actual room was an A1 experience. I loved every moment I was on the property.  Luxury may be an understatement with what I experienced.

reviews.title: Sister 21st Birthday 🎉
reviews.text: 10 out of 10! Not only was this place stunning it offered luxury shopping along with great amenities all in one place! The decor was beautiful, both in the lobbies and bedroom. We had a great view which was towards the mountains so the sunrise and sunset was really nice. The pool was very very nice. This is a family friendly resort but trust me it wasn't bad.Even with the kiddos around it was still great vibes. I loved the bathroom the bathtub will have you falling asleep! Each room also came with a robe and complimentary slippers. Customer service was top tier as well! If you thinking about stor here do it! Promise you won't regret it

reviews.title: mean service
reviews.text: The casino managers are mean, they don't care about the customers. The machine are not functional. The hotel is under construction, made a lot noise.

reviews.title: Love This Place
reviews.text: There are very few hotels/resorts that I will stay at and not leave the property. This is one of them. Excellent overall experience with exceptional restaurants (Ito, Mother Wolf, Kyu, and Washing Potato) and a world class spa. .

reviews.title: Overall a Great Resort with a Few Issues
reviews.text: I’ve been to this resort twice and can truly say it’s my favorite on the Strip.The design is timeless and elegant….something you don’t find much in Vegas and with an equally nice crowd.The rooms were a highlight.  The resort is relatively new and everything feels fresh and clean.  The beds were sublimely comfortable.The location is a bit north of all of the action on the strip, which was a good thing.  There’s plenty of space to stretch out and breathe here.Probably the biggest negative was the lack of in -room coffee machines.  For the caliber of hotel, this was a big miss for the hotel and mission impossible to get a quick cup of coffee in the morning.  The resort should immediately add in room coffee machines as lines for the coffee shop were quite long.    Also, adding an on-site Starbucks/second coffeeshop  would be a no-brainer. The spa and gym are were also very good and another highlight.   Although the gym was well-equipped, it lacked a lot of basic machines (bicep curl) and closed everyday at 7PM…really unacceptable.  If the above issues are addressed, I would definitely stay here again.  Otherwise I might return to the Durango out in the suburbs.

reviews.title: Nice views is a pretty place
reviews.text: Is great pretty place they need to work in little thinks but over all good experience all the food places are great nice front desk and gym team

reviews.title: Outstanding
reviews.text: This is a lovely hotel on the north end of the Strip.   It is a 30 minute walk or short cab ride to Sphere. The property is very large, bright and airy.  Many of the rooms have excellent views, and they are spacious and modern.The fitness center is excellent, essentially a full gym, the pool area is lovely.  WiFi is fast.  There are many outstanding places to eat and a good food court as well.Finally, this is a price performer compared to other hotels of similar quality on the Strip.

reviews.title: Major security problem mishandled
reviews.text: I don't have often write reviews here, but I experienced an extreme security problem here that has left me shaken and incredulous. I was walking up to the guest elevators area, where there is a podium where security checks key cards for guests. A man walked up to me as I was approaching it, put his arm around me, and asked me to "have some fun." I said no and kept walking. He squeezed his arm around me tighter and said, "Come up to my room. I'll take you up." I pushed away and approached the security podium. He told security that I was his wife, was drunk, and he was taking me up to our room. I told security I didn't know him. Security then asked him if he was a guest. He said yes, showed his room key card, and gave them his room number. They then asked if I was a guest. I said yes, and showed my key card. They then asked for my room number, which I provided. They then asked me for picture ID.. They did not ask the man for his ID. I showed them my driver's license. They then said that I couldn't go up to my room. I was very confused, and security allowed him to keep squeezing his arm around me and trying to pull me up to his room. The restrooms were around a bend from this area, and I pulled away, telling security I'm going to the bathroom. I went to the women's restroom and called my work colleague, who was also in the casino. He came to meet me by the bathroom door and walked me back to security. When we got there, the creepy man was standing there waiting for me and saying I'm taking her to our room. My friend intervened and talked to security. Security allowed this man to get all the way to the elevator bank trying to get me to his room. At some point security decided to escore me up, and at that point the guy hopped in the elevators. Security escorted me to my room, where I bolted the door. Shortly therafter, there was banging on my door. I looked out the peep hole, and it was the guy. He would not have known my room number if security had not asked me for it in front of him. I called security and reported it. I then called another colleague who was also staying in our hotel. She stayed on the phone with me while he was banging on the door. As the knocking escalated, and no one showed up, she also called security from her room. Security gave her a hard time, saying that the call needed to come from the room that needed help. More time passed, and as I looked out the peep hole, the man had sat down outside my room. I called security again, and they said that they had sent someone up there to talk to him, but the guy said that he made an innocent mistake of knocking on the wrong room, so there wasn't a problem. Unfortunately the knocking continued and he was still out there. Much time passed with about 6-7 calls to security. Eventually security did come up, and while the security person was standing at my door, he received a message in his ear piece that the man was in the stairwell. They went to apprehend him. More time passed, and I couldn't get answers. Eventually security came back and said that they would move me to a different room. They said that they didn't apprehend him in the stairwell. Security told me to call the front desk to get the room assignment and then they would give me a security escort to a different part of the hotel. I then made many, many calls to the front desk. One person said, "What's wrong with the room" and another said I had to come to the desk to get the information (and I had to explain that security had told me to stay locked in my room. Eventually, and hours had passed by now, the front desk manager called to say that she was sending security up with a card key and new room to move me. Security then showed up and asked, "Where are we going?" He had no key card and didn't know where we were going. He called downstairs while we waited for a long time in the hallway to figure out what to do. Eventually I was moved to a different part of the hotel, many hours later. This should not be allowed to happen in a casino. When a woman says "I don't know this man," there is no world in which you question that. You do not ask a woman in front of a man who is squeezing his arm around you and pushing to provide her room number in front of him. And you don't take hours to solve a problem while a man creepily sits outside a woman's hotel room. It was a harrowing experience and no one seemed to care. The hotel is beautiful and we enjoyed some wonderful dinners here and afternoons by the pool, but no matter how nice a hotel may be, it's useless if not safe for women.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: Careful if you book this hotel through American Express Platinum fine hotels and resorts, you might get there and they will wipe out your benefits. Platinum benefits do not book your airline at the same time you will lose your platinum benefits

reviews.title: Fontainebleau 06/22-06/25
reviews.text: Had a three night comp-stay (6/22/6-25) in a Gold room.  Observations follow:1.	Property remains beautiful.  Pretty much spotless!  Well done by all of the nameless (perhaps if you don’t notice) folks working tirelessly to keep things that way.2.	Table limits where $15 during the day, $25 evening for blackjack.  (Big change from $50 evening limits at the Wynn).  3-card poker opened at 9pm, at $15.  Sign of the times!3.	Multiple craps tables open all the time.4.	Resort and casino seemed busier than prior stays.5.	Miami Slice pizza good as always.  Capons Chicken, Won’t try again as chicken was only "meh" for me  .(only staff that asked me for rewards card to add points.  That staff member should be rewarded!).  Chez Bon Bon had usual quality offerings.  Smashed Almond Croissant was a genuine treat!  Tropical fruit cup also delicious!6.	Don’s Prime!  What can I say?  I have tried several LV steakhouses and this is my favorite!  The service is my stand-out…always attentive, professional, never intrusive…truly a cut above.  They offered a prix fixe (?) summer special, three courses for $105 (with a wine pairing for $65).  I chose the crab cake, with the most delicious sauce, the 9oz filet (side of creamed spinach – extra) and the best crème brule I have ever tasted!  The wine pairing included a delicious Heidsick Bubbles, A wonderful California cab and a lovely Sauternes.  Could not have been happier!  (and a good value compared to regular menu prices).  AND THE SERVICE!  I dare say you will not find a better team in Las Vegas!7.	Had very good fish tacos at the sports bar.8.	Let me say again that all of the staff had a smile, a greeting and were always working hard to make the guest experience top notch!  ( I state this as a long time Wynn/Encore guest, who appreciates great service.)9.	I mostly play slots and this casino has everything I look for!  Always some new games to try (and try I did!).  Also, good share of classic three reel/low volatility games).  As mentioned above, blackjack and craps were always open.  Three card poker, open at 9pm during the week.  Wonder 4 poker, weekends only.10.	I really like this property and hope more folks will give it a try!  It’s a real joy!Happy to answer questions!SteveO.

reviews.title: Best hotel and resort on the strip by far.
reviews.text: Everything about the Fontainebleau is top notch.  The rooms, restaurants, gaming and even the parking.  Great air conditioning in the rooms when compared to competitors.

reviews.title: Anyone can do vegas, but the Fontainbleu is next level comfort.
reviews.text: Fontainbleu is an exquisite exerience from the grand entrance to the impeccable rooms. Everything about the resort is next level from the cocktail program to the gaming. The pool(s) are beautiful and relaxing with cabana's and daybeds that we really enjoyed.

reviews.title: Opulent accommodations and excellent staff
reviews.text: I have only experienced this level of courtesy and professionalism from staff at one other place, and it was a Disney resort.  Everyone was incredibly polite and going above and beyond to make sure guests were having a good stay.  The accommodations were opulent (in my experience, anyway) and I had a terrific view.  The food was expensive (welcome to Vegas) but delicious.  I'd highly recommend this spot.

reviews.title: Worth the money!
reviews.text: It was a beautiful hotel!  Everything was clean and in order.  Beds were fluffy, not firm, which I liked!  Water pressure was spot on in the shower, but be careful, the water is hot if you don't test it before you enter.  I have some advice if you're on a budget, but still want this luxurious hotel:  If you're a coffee drinker, pack your own personal coffee pot and coffee pods.  I got mine from Walmart for only $16! Their rooms do not have them.  I also recommend getting snacks and water from the Walgreens across the street.  Unless you're rich, don't eat and drink from their mini bar!  There are ice and water machines on each floor, so you may want bring something to drink out of, like a thermos.  All in all, it was a wonderful stay!

reviews.title: Best Hotel in Vegas
reviews.text: This hotel is next level - Better rooms - Better service - Better food - Better ambiance- Just overall Better than anything else Vegas offers right now.

reviews.title: Nice Room Hotel but need to improve in Casino Gaming
reviews.text: The hotel facility was nice and the room was clean.  The only negative was there was no variety of Black Jack games.  The payout of blackjack is 6to5 instead of 3to2, no double decks games.The Ultimate Texas Holdem has the rules that the Dealer is getting the first card instead of the last one, which give the Player more concerns.

reviews.title: Stay at the Fontainbleau
reviews.text: The hotel was BEAUTIFUL and I loved their attention to detail (a fun game was finding the bowties in the decor. They're in everything!). The staff were friendly and helpful. I stayed in a "Royal Suite Strip Best View" room for 6 nights. The room was a nice size with 2 full bathrooms. The decor and furnishing in the room were beautiful as well. The view was GREAT! The bed and robes were extremely comfortable. All in all, I think it was worth it and enjoyed my stay BUT when I first got to the room, I noticed right away it hadn't been cleaned thoroughly. There were rice grains and paper from an open sugar packet around the kitchen sink, a piece of tissue in the fridge and melted water and a plastic bag in the ice bucket. This was surprising because I expect a freshly cleaned room from any establishment I choose to stay in, but even more so when I'm staying in a suite at a 5-star hotel.  I called the front desk, and they said they would have someone come up and "take care of it". I asked the agent to send them in a half an hour as I'd be gone, and they could have the rooms to themselves and was told my request was noted. Despite that, housekeeping showed up 5 minutes later, picked up the garbage, emptied the ice bucket, sprayed air freshener and left. After witnessing this, I took sometime later the next morning to more closely examine the room and further confirmed the room was not being cleaned properly. There was hair and debris in the corners of the room, the 'vanity packs' had been opened and left in the container and the AC vent was full of dust. I called the front desk again to explain the issues in full detail, hoping someone would understand my concerns and the principle behind it. I spoke with Renee, who expressed she understood my concerns, would send someone up to do a thorough cleaning and I could expect a call from the Manager of Housekeeping. She also stated that I had received $75 in resort credit towards food and beverages, for my inconvenience. Despite me requesting a specific time, I got a call from housekeeping 10 minutes later to say they were outside and had to request again they come back once I had left. I was still able to note the same exact debris in the same areas after the "thorough" cleaning, received no call from the manager and didn't notice any credits on my final bill. Only after this cleaning did I notice there were amenities (toothbrush, razor, mouthwash, etc.) provided that had not been during the "initial" cleaning. This was of no importance due to the fact that I didn't use any of the provided items but further proves the room was not being taken care of as it should have been. Room service was a bit slow (minimum hour wait, even just for wings) but it was the weekend, and the hotel was pretty busy.

reviews.title: Great Start but needs to fix bathroom aerators.
reviews.text: Had a weeklong stay in a Panorama Suite on this trip and had a weeklong stay in a Noble Suite on my trip in March of 2025.First thing to note is the arrival experience.  The valet can be extremely busy.  Drop off was smooth on both trips, but the traffic in front was a bit rough.  When you enter the resort, you are greeted by beautiful floral display.  To your right there is a VIP/Gold and above check in desk.  They are very militant about that desk.  On my first trip I had to go to the main check in and though the line was long the process was smooth and acceptable.  On my second trip I was up to Gold (Reward Status) and when I tried to use the VIP check in, I was told I wasn't allowed.  I had to login to my account on my phone to prove that I could use the VIP line which no one was in.  The standard check in was 30 plus people deep.  Even after I showed her, she was very snooty like I didn't belong.  The VIP check in was excellent (Aria Sky Suites level).  I had originally booked a Regal Suite and upgraded to the Panorama.  It was well worth it.The resort elevators are a short walk on tile from check in which is great.  Nothing worse than dragging your roller bag across carpet through a casino (Best reason to get a Wynn Tower Suite).  The Casino ceilings are super high, and it feels so open and comfortable compared to older resorts (Think Paris).  The elevators are quick and well thought out.Once to the room it was beautifully appointed and had amazing views.  Plenty of space to unpack and spread out.  The Panorama is an excellent choice for a couple that have different sleep schedules.  The living area is a good distance from the bedroom and very comfortable.  Room service coffee at the dining table or the living area is perfect.As a frequent traveler I can say my biggest beef with resorts often are the showers.  The water pressure in the shower is very impressive and makes the stay worth every penny. (If you have ever stayed at the Cosmopolitan, you know what I mean about the shower.  Hugh beautiful showers that have zero water pressure.)  My beef with the Fontainbleau is the bathroom sink aerator.  It puts the water out as a spray and it's a big miss.  Hard to rinse a toothbrush or razor.The Casino is great.  Plenty of table games.  I'm a craps player and they have both Craps and Crapless open most of the time.  They have a Bar that opens at 5:00 that has a Crapless table and quality drink service and is open every night ($25.00 Min).  Food options are plentiful and fantastic.  Spend the money and go to Don's Steakhouse.  Tavern Sports Bar has great food as well as the second floor food court (Possibly best burger in Vegas).The pool.  I did a Cabana on Friday and it was a great experience and the value was there.  Went down on Saturday to spend a couple of hours and there wasn't a single chair available on the entire pool deck.  Lots of empty chairs with Towels on them people were doing the old reserve for later move.  They need to get better about policing such activity (Wynn is the best at stopping this behavior).I would be remiss if I didn't say to stop by the No Where bar and get a drink from Reggie.  Best Espresso Martini I have ever had (and I've had way too many lol).

reviews.title: Highly recommend.
reviews.text: It was a great experience. The room was immaculate as was the service. It was a quick couple’s getaway weekend, so we mostly stayed in the hotel for our time. We ate at Mother Wolf and got drinks at Bleau Bar and I will be going back to both.

reviews.title: Class & Comfort in the Fontainebleau
reviews.text: Modern, classy establishment. Not cheap, but worth the splurge. Easy to navigate, unlike many of the strip hotels/casinos. It didn’t take half a day to reach self-parking! Well ventilated and little smoking on the casino floor. Courteous and friendly staff. Rooms were bright, spacious, and comfortable. Nice amenities in rooms: Clothes steamer, plush robes, slippers, toiletries, and chocolates! Bath tub was big enough to invite a couple of seals to do laps.

reviews.title: Go to Fontainebleau! You will love it!
reviews.text: If you are looking for a fabulous hotel with all the amenities you could want, you should absolutely check out Fontainebleau. It's beautiful, full of high-end shopping, restaurants, has a beautiful pool(s) and very comfortable, stylish rooms. I had a king room with strip view and it was only about $300/night (before taxes and fees) which was excellent! Room service food was fantastic (get the burger!) as was the food at our business conference. The casino isn't very big so if you are an avid gambler, this may not be your favorite spot, but if you enjoy playing the slots, there are plenty of those. When I come back to Vegas for pleasure in the future, I will probably stay here. I loved it!

reviews.title: Splurge on yourself!
reviews.text: The Fountaineblue in Las Vegas is an absolute splurge that everyone should experience at least once. The hotel, rooms and restaurants are on point. The Lapis Spa was an incredible experience from the Odessy massage to their saunas experiences and the salt room, exquisite.  Definitely worth every cent.

reviews.title: Spend your summer at Fontainebleau...now!
reviews.text: Amazing from start to finish. Checked in early, my room type wasn't available, but they found me something that was and waived early check in fee. Spent 3 days at the incredible pools - best in town with lots of seating and many shaded seats. Food was amazing at Washing Potato for dim sum and Papi steak was pricey but delicious. Got a $100 dining credit for stay. Amazing room rate deal as a member too. Amazing service at both. Slots and video poker were great fun and many bonuses a a couple good wins!

reviews.title: The most elegant resort in Vegas!
reviews.text: The most elegant and relaxing resort experience in Vegas! The only place we will stay from now on. Our suite was gorgeous and comfortable. Food was terrific, especially at Papi Steak. Casino was beautiful and welcoming. Pool was refreshing. We highly recommend visiting the brand new "Hall of Excellence" which showcases incredible memorabilia from the worlds of sports and entertainment. A must see!

reviews.title: Nice place with great service! Pool costs are too high
reviews.text: Fantastic hotel and casino with a fantastic pool. The only drawback is the very expensive drink menu at the pool. It out prices its competitors and that makes a difference for us that hang at the pool all day!

reviews.title: Top-tier Vegas establishment
reviews.text: Cleanest hotel, and casino in Vegas. I’ve been to Vegas about 25 times and this place is amazing. Tried about six different restaurants and shops and they were all excellent

reviews.title: Absolutely the Best ‘Bet’ in Las Vegas!
reviews.text: This is an updated review because I have since spent another couple days here, and I’m so further blown away that I just wanted to revise and add. My Las Vegas experience thus far consists of staying at the Mandalay Bay, The Four Seasons and the Cosmopolitan. This new Fontainebleu hotel, Las Vegas is in such a different league; there truly is no comparison.    I have been very fortunate in my lifetime to have stayed at some of the best hotels and resorts around the world, and this particular new Las Vegas hotel, when it comes to checking off all the boxes that could possibly be checked, takes the cake.   The location is fantastic, the aesthetics are unparalleled, all the food venues that we tried were absolutely spectacular. Every employee we encountered was phenomenal; and there are thousands of people that work here…    The room was beautiful, incredibly comfortable with a phenomenal mattress, excellent linens, excellent air-conditioning, fantastic shower water pressure, not to mention we were up on the 68th floor, so the view was extraordinary and it was as quiet as can be. I’ve been an Equinox all-access gym member for years, and the fully equipped health club here on the second floor is as nice (if not nicer) than any of the Equinox gyms around the country. Even the casino was fun, of which I usually do not spend any time in. And they have an enormous, clean and safe, easy-to-navigate through self-parking facility attached to the hotel which is just fantastic for those of us who sometimes prefer not to be fussed over at check-in or check out.  This hotel helped me fall in love with Las Vegas this trip, and we are happy that we are moving back to the West Coast so we’ll be able to come here with frequency for a quick getaways.  I truly cannot recommend this hotel enough, not to mention that it can be even less costly than some of the other, above mentioned Las Vegas hotels that I’ve stayed at previously.  Special mention to Delfa at Front-Desk/Check-in, she is exceptional, a true gem; the hotel is lucky to have her.  Also special mentioned to Ashley in The Tavern.    Thank you Team Fontainebleau, we look forward to returning soon!

reviews.title: One-Star Review: Disappointing Customer Service at Fontainebleau Las Vegas
reviews.text: As a local military member, I frequent resorts up and down the Strip, and I've consistently experienced outstanding service everywhere—except at the Fontainebleau. While it's a beautiful resort, the customer service, particularly concerning military members and locals, is severely lacking.Every other hotel on the Strip acknowledges and appreciates military service by placing us on a higher tier, a privilege we never take for granted. The Fontainebleau, however, uses the same tired excuse that they don't offer such a program yet, despite having been open for a considerable amount of time. They also fall short by not offering tier matching, a common practice among other casinos.My family and I may not be high rollers, but we regularly enjoy dining, shows, and concerts at Strip resorts. Given the well-publicized issues Fontainebleau has had with customer loyalty, you'd think they'd make more of an effort to improve their standing with locals. Instead, it feels like they're just digging a deeper hole.With so many other excellent options available on the Strip that genuinely value their guests, especially the local military community, I'll unfortunately be passing on the Fontainebleau this year.

reviews.title: Not a 5 star resort or experience.  Too much cost cutting to try and stay afloat but that has ruined things.
reviews.text: Not a 5 star resort or experience.  Too much cost cutting to try and stay afloat but that has ruined things.

reviews.title: Top notch resort
reviews.text: We had a great time here. If you are looking to be with a mature crowd away from the chaos of the strip this is the place to go! The food was excellent and the amenities were on point. Room was spacious with excellent views. Conveniently located with easy cheap taxi rides to wherever you need to go.

reviews.title: Move over, Cosmopolitan
reviews.text: This might be my new favorite hotel in Vegas. You feel like you're in the lap of luxury as soon as you walk in.The common areas are beautiful and the casino is great. I was pleasantly surprised that some of the slots and table games had low minimums. Of course, if you want high limits, there's plenty of those.The pools were nice. They're family friendly, but not to the point that I felt annoyed. There's a 21+ pool too, but it was dead most of the time. That's fine though, as I was mainly there for the hot tub. I didn't get a chance to go to Liv, but it sounded like a vibe. Maybe next time.

reviews.title: Best hotel in Vegas!
reviews.text: This casino and hotel are as nice as any of the luxury hotels on the strip, and a much better value. Rooms are large and new and the staff is too notch.

reviews.title: Best spot on the strip!
reviews.text: I know it's a little ways down the strip, but I have stayed at Fontainbleu 3 times now, and each visit was exceptional. The staff is friendly and helpful, the rooms are clean and beautiful, and the restaurants (especially Mother Wolf and Miami Slice) are some of the best in Vegas.

reviews.title: FB wknd get away
reviews.text: Hotel was everything we expected it to be. It is at the end of the strip but has so many amenities you don’t need to leave the resort at all. We had the strip view from our room, can even see the Dome and room was slightly larger than other king rooms. Restaurants (Papi Steak, Mother Wolf, and Vida) plus in room dining were also all great! 21+ pools could use livelier music choices but all in all, great stay!

reviews.title: The best hotel in Vegas
reviews.text: The Fontainebleaus Hotel is by far the most beautiful hotel in Vegas. We would book it again and again. The rooms, the staff, the pool area, the casino, the gym it's just all right. Thanks for this fantastic stay!

reviews.title: Really fantastic hotel.
reviews.text: Very nice hotel. Great ambiance. Excellent service   Great food and amenitiesBest gymExpensive with some nickel and dime charges that are unnecessary at this price point ($10 to deliver wine glasses to the room)

reviews.title: Luxe Aesthetic, Clean Vibe, and a Bit Out of the Way
reviews.text: Fountainbleau is a good option if you're looking to get away from the chaos of the central Vegas Strip. It's a large, modern resort located at the far end of the Strip, kind of off on its own. It has just about everything you'd expect—plenty of restaurants, bars, a casino, spa, shops, a big pool complex, and LIV (note: both the club and pool have entrance fees).Once you're there, it really doesn't make a lot of sense to head back down to the busy parts of Vegas. It’s more of a self-contained experience—convenient in some ways, isolating in others.Pros:- The room was spacious, stylish, and clean. Easily one of the nicer rooms I’ve stayed in for the price.- The whole place is bright, smoke-free, and doesn’t have that heavy, stale-air feel most Vegas hotels have.- Pool area is impressive, and there's an adults-only pool that’s actually peaceful (rare for Vegas).- If you book through Amex Fine Hotels & Resorts, you get a few solid perks like breakfast and early check-in/late checkout.Cons:- It’s far from most of the action. You’re looking at a longer Uber ride to Strip spots like Bellagio, Caesars, etc.- Restaurants were pricey—not just “Vegas pricey,” but noticeably higher than similar places on the Strip. Papi Steak in particular felt like style over substance.Avoid:We were invited to make a reservation at the Poodle Room, which is a “hidden” lounge they pitch as exclusive with the best view of the Strip and Sphere. Honestly, it was nice but totally dead. Drinks were overpriced, and the vibe just wasn’t there. Wouldn’t recommend unless you're just curious.

reviews.title: A Luxury Respite on the South Strip
reviews.text: First class venue removed from the crowded North end of the Strip. If you looking for upscale elegance and quiet this is great venue — except when LIV Beach is happening on Saturday afternoon.

reviews.title: Best Experience
reviews.text: Besst Resortg every - amazingt and A+ from check in to check out to Rewards Program - it was excellent all through - I would not hesitate to receommend this resort to all - try it and u will fall in love ! Rooms are modern and classy with all amenities thorougly thought thru

reviews.title: Not worth the price, better options south
reviews.text: Rooms are pretty nice. Tough location to walk other places. You’re stuck w captive restaurants which are fine but not great. Great gym. Service overall below what you’d expect at other similar venues. For example we had no hot water one morning after waiting 5 minutes. Called and they said the hotel was full. Wait longer. Ok, fine, but that doesn’t happen at Holiday Inn when I’m paying $800 less per night. Overall it’s fine but I wouldn’t go back. Better places if you’re happy spending $1000 a night.

reviews.title: Very impressive
reviews.text: The best stay we have had in Vegas to date. Everyone is extremely helpful and friendly and the rooms are very clean. The beds were so comfortable it made me want one for our home:) Next time I’d like to try more of the restaurants but we did dine in The Tavern food was very good. Definitely looking forward to our next visit

reviews.title: Overall Would Stay Again - but definitely areas for improvement
reviews.text: As a Front Office Manager with several years in the hospitality industry, I always appreciate experiencing other hotels and wanted to share my feedback on my recent stay at the Fontainebleau Las Vegas. I was in Vegas celebrating my 28th birthday and attended two shows at LIV and LIV Beach which were conveniently located at this property which is why we chose to stay at the Fontainebleau. Positives:The property itself is stunning—modern, luxurious, and beautifully designed. We had a great view of the pool despite being only on the 8th floor, and the key-access requirement for guest elevators was a fantastic touch for security. Pool access was easy, and the beverage service was on point. The Promenade food hall had a solid variety of options and was convenient for quick, quality bites. I also want to give a big shout-out to housekeeping—our room was serviced exceptionally well on the day we requested it.Areas for Improvement:Unfortunately, several aspects of the in-room experience fell short. The drapes didn’t fully close, the rainfall shower head wasn’t functioning, one of the lamps didn’t work, and the beverage cooler barely chilled the drinks we purchased. I brought this up at check-out, and while I understand issues can arise, a simple apology or acknowledgment from the front desk staff would’ve made a difference—especially since these should have been caught during room inspections.Additionally, the service from most staff members (excluding the valet team, who were great) lacked warmth and engagement. Eye contact and a friendly tone go a long way, but we experienced minimal guest interaction. Even at check in, and there not being a line, our check in contained minimal conversation which is a great way to connect with the guest and start their trip on the right foot. We also had checked our luggage and went to get it before heading upstairs and said we could bring it ourselves so the gentleman got our cert and began unloading all our items, keep in mind we had 5 bags and a box for the two of us and when asked if we could use the cart we got a fairly rude response of “no, that’s why I asked if you wanted to bring your stuff or if you wanted us to bring it up.” I understand not wanting guests taking the carts because they may never make it back for other guests, but it would have been appreciated had that been made clear when we requested our bags to begin with. We could not have brought all the items by ourself so we had to go up to the room then call the bell desk to have our items brought up and when I gave the representative our ticket number and room number he called us a different guests name… this caused immediate concern as to if we would be getting our bags. Ultimately, we did about 30 minutes later, the agent called me back and said “hello, just wanted to let you know we switched the names on your room so you are all set now”, shouldn’t that have been immediately done when we were checked into the room and given keys? Another instance was a call to request bandaids resulted in a short, dismissive response and a 25-minute wait.Overall, Fontainebleau has the potential to offer an exceptional guest experience, but a stronger focus on room maintenance and genuine service culture would elevate it significantly. The property is stunning and we did overall love the stay, but the interactions we had with the staff both at the beginning of our stay and towards the end, did sour it a little bit. But, that being said, it is a newer property and still figuring it out. Our experience would not deter us from staying again.

reviews.title: "Overpriced, Unsanitary, and Fraudulent Charges — Avoid at All Costs
reviews.text: 🔥 **Fontainebleau Las Vegas Review**⭐ **1 Star****"Overpriced, Unsanitary, and Fraudulent Charges — Avoid at All Costs"**My recent stay at **Fontainebleau Las Vegas** was one of the worst hotel experiences I’ve ever had — and I travel often. I booked two rooms (one prepaid, one financed through Expedia) expecting luxury and received nothing but **stress, filth, and unauthorized charges**.Upon arrival, I was told to pay an **additional $850 per room as a “deposit,”** even though one room was paid in full and the other was secured through Expedia. When we entered the rooms, we were horrified:* Hair shavings in the sink* Dirty rugs* Hair on the bathroom floor* A **used tissue** left in the nightstandWe checked out in **less than 24 hours**, and I was assured by the front desk that I’d only be charged the resort fee and taxes — totaling $62.50 per room. **Minutes later**, I discovered **$604 per room had been charged to my card** without explanation.I immediately returned to the front desk and was told the charges were a mistake and that the refund would be processed. **No refund has ever arrived.**I reported this to **Expedia**, who then blamed the hotel — while the hotel blamed Expedia. Neither took accountability, and both have caused me emotional and financial frustration.Fontainebleau may look flashy from the outside, but behind the scenes, it’s mismanaged and dishonest.**Unclean rooms. Dishonest billing. Rude management. No integrity.**Avoid this hotel — there’s nothing luxurious about being scammed.

reviews.title: I’ll never stay anywhere else in Vegas!
reviews.text: By far the best LV hotel I’ve ever experienced. The vibe is light and bright. Everything is CLEAN. The rooms are amazing (get the Strip view) and the shower was to die for. We loved getting a private cabana at the Oasis pool - VIP check-in, outstanding service/food and welcome shade. The entire place is amazing. Don’t miss their French patisserie for an early morning coffee and croissant.

reviews.title: Great stay
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful with a mountain of fresh roses in the lobby that get changed often (we're told).  High end shops and restaurants are all over. The rooms are big and clean. The AC is a bit loud but not enough to prevent me from sleeping. We were on the 28th floor so we had a great view. Speaking of views, the Sphere can be seen when standing outside. Fontainebleau is located a few miles away from the common/popular hotels on the strip. We Uber most of the time but it is a walkable distance.  Aside from how expensive the restaurants are, the area where our room was located had a peculiar/unpleasant smell that never went away. I should've asked for a different room but instead I dealt with it because I didn't smell it inside the room.

reviews.title: A must stay in Vegas
reviews.text: If you are looking for a new, clean, and exciting hotel in Vegas, this is where you want to stay. The restaurants options are endless and the hotel staff are so friendly. We only had to leave our hotel for a few business meetings.

reviews.title: Conference at Fontainebleau
reviews.text: Fantastic property, both the rooms and conference area. The shops and eatery's were top notch. Little loud but overall great experience.

reviews.title: Best spot on the strip!
reviews.text: Our experience was the best we have ever had on the strip. We found our new home! From the dealers to the restaurants, not a better place to spend a weekend with friends!

reviews.title: Excellent hotel great tourism, highlighting its concept and luxury in each of its facilities. Don't stop visiting
reviews.text: Excellent hotel great tourism, highlighting its concept and luxury in each of its facilities. Don't stop visiting

reviews.title: Luxurious destination resort!
reviews.text: Exceptional experience!  Fontainebleau is a destination resort, with luxurious rooms, restaurants, and pools.  The Nowhere Lounge features top jazz musicians nightly.  All of the staff ate well dressed and professional with a smile.  Cheers!

reviews.title: Love the Miami Fontainebleau, but the Fontainebleau Las Vegas Needs Major Help!
reviews.text: I expected the hotel to have a 5 star experience like the Miami hotel, but this one was soulless and without question the most painful luxury hotel bed I've ever experienced.  I'm in Vegas a ton, and it would take a major change to go back to the Fontainebleau.  I've never had a luxury hotel where I leave with neck and shoulder pain due to a bad mattress and specifically awful pillows.  This hotel has an amazing shell and bones, but it feels soulless and needs an internal refresh.

reviews.title: Fountainbleu June 2025
reviews.text: Rooms are amazing-fresh and new. Super clean. Modern and up to date. Great views of the sphere and the city in general. Checking in was very easy. Jeremy at the check in desk was awesome. The casino floor is super clean and well lit. Restrooms on the casino floor were clean. The Tavern restaurant/sportsbook has amazing food. Definitely recommend the Prime Rib French Dip sandwich. It was the best French dip I think I have ever had. The auju was perfect. The meat was so tender and finely sliced. Definitely two thumbs up. Parking garage is super easy to get in and out of. There are several other casinos within walking distance. We loved this place!

reviews.title: A Beautiful Hotel in a Less Desirable Area
reviews.text: This hotel is luxurious and the rooms meet the standard.  Positive points are that parking is free for guests.  (I read it somewhere on the website, but it wasn't that obvious.)  The location is irs main negative.  That area of the stripstill has elements  of seediness.

reviews.title: Great Experience
reviews.text: Beautiful hotel.  Fantastic service.  Food was impeccable.  Would highly recommend for a person looking for luxury without the nonsense further down the strip.  Very classy experience without the high price of the Wynn.  The pool was a great mix of families and singles.

reviews.title: The best hotel in Las Vegas, Fontainebleau
reviews.text: Great in...- Service- Room - Overall decoration- AtmosphereMy first time in Vegas and this is the first impression I've got from this city, Fontainebleau Las Vegas! Thank to my team who decided choosing this hotel for 9 nights. Moreover, the bar, casino and food court were so great!

reviews.title: Not all new is good
reviews.text: A hotel that is still really green in service and attitude. Has a lot to work on before competing with the other hotels on the Strip. Beds were super uncomfortable, service was terrible, zero politeness.They don't try to make an effort on guests experience.

reviews.title: Hotel/Casino in Las Vegas, NV
reviews.text: Overall a pretty, clean and spacious casino!  Didn’t stay here but came to check out their casino and grab lunch Sunday.  La Fontaine is a good place to eat at!  Casino wise, lots of slot machines and tables to play—wasn’t crowded at all (daytime).  One thing that needs improvement is cocktail service—we played at the slot machines for a while and no cocktail waitress came by for drinks—all the other casinos we’d been to all weekend had plenty of servers come by.Location wise, this is a bit far from the main area strip and is a bit more secluded so it’s not as lively/energetic area.  They offer valet which was $40.  Lobby had beautiful pink red roses as decor, so pretty!

reviews.title: Fantastic hotel experience!
reviews.text: Fantastic place! Highly recommended. Beautiful, clean, quiet, excellent customer service, fantastic food and different options. It is far enough from the main, loud, super busy, and sometimes dirty strip, but also close enough to go anywhere. Swimming pools are also great!

reviews.title: Elegance and class is what this hotel is .
reviews.text: Elegant and classy, from the pool to the service everything was fabulous. the restaurants are phenomenal. It’s at the end of the strip which is great because it’s not crazy busy with people coming to look at it. We absolutely loved it. We will be back

reviews.title: Best resort in Vegas.
reviews.text: Excellent stay overall. I will be back.They bend over backwards to make sure you are completely satisfied. Rooms are a pleasure to stay in,everything is provided. The views were awesome from my room on the 50th floor.I will highly recommend this resort.

reviews.title: Best hotel in Vegas
reviews.text: Best hotel in Vegas , clean, beautiful, modern, great restaurants, nice common areas . I would definitely recommend this hotel to friends and I would definitely come back for my next visit. The rooms are spacious and very comfortable. The best hotel.

reviews.title: 2 star service, 5 star price
reviews.text: We got a great deal on our room; if I had paid list price on my room I would NOT be writing a three star review - it would be much less. Our room was supposed to be ready at 3 and it wasn't ready until nearly 5pm. The check-in desk was kind but when we asked what the issue was they couldn't give us an answer and offered nothing for the inconvenience besides keys to the pool (which we would have had regardless). We travel fairly extensively and I honestly can't think of a time that our room wasn't ready on time and certainly not 2 hours late. The hotel is beautiful and clean, staff is very kind, but I think they're understaffed and the air in our room wasn't working well. We ate at Vida for breakfast and sat at the bar, I had to ask the bartender multiple times for refills of water; my cup was sitting right where he was working - it was a little annoying to have to draw it to his attention. But again, I think he was just overwhelmed/overworked. The staff was doing a terrible job checking keycards to get into the pool and to get up to the rooms. We went to the pool and ordered tequila, soda water, lime with extra limes and got lime juice with tequila in it (one lime). Our waitress was wonderful and did make it right though :). I would have been WILDLY upset if I had paid the normal going rate for the type of service we experienced.

reviews.title: Much like Cosmopolitan
reviews.text: As a VIP customer, I found that the treatment at Fountainbleau was not as accommodating as other hotels like Bellagio/MGM or Wynn. The room was adequate at best and the bath products were used and had not been changed from the previous guest. The hotel is much like the Cosmopolitan in that it is for a young crowd not a gambling crowd.

reviews.title: Had a great time
reviews.text: Very comfortable rooms and happy with the way everything went service was very nice too the pizza and tacos are amazing too id definitely go again if I’d stay anywhere in Las Vegas it would be here and the pool too it’s very nice and big service there was great too

reviews.title: Fresh and fun
reviews.text: Gorgeous hotel with fresh, modern amenities,  beautiful layout, and decor. A breath of fresh air on the strip. I stayed for a short weekend trip and enjoyed the spa which offered a serene, relaxing and luxe experience. I will absolutely be back and highly recommend staying here!

reviews.title: We love the Fontainebleau !!
reviews.text: Really fabulous  hotel.  Much less smoky smelling than other Vegas hotels. They work hard to keep that smell out of the hotel and we love that.  Fabulous employees.
